newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Antenna Hungaria gets HUF 2.5 bln cash injection.
newsitem.headline: Antenna Hungaria gets HUF 2.5 bln cash injection.

text.p: National broadcaster Antenna Hungaria (AH) will get a 2.5 billion forints cash injection earmarked for developments needed this year for media privatisation, the government said on Thursday.
"The money can only be spent on funding four investments in 1997," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference after the weekly cabinet meeting.

The money will come from privatisation agency APV Rt's reorganisation fund and will be used for a capital increase to be approved at an extraordinary general meeting at the end of January, a statement said.

Hungary has offered 10-year concessions for two national Television and two radio channels and state-owned AH, which broadcasts all of Hungary's radio and TV programmes has to upgrade the infrastructure.

AH needs to develop the infrastructure for broadcasting of a national TV-channel, two national FM-channels and to build a sattelite uplink for state television's Channel 2, which will go on satellite once its frequency has been taken over by private television.
Kiss added that AH cannot use the amount to solve its liquidity problems.
AH is due some 2.5 billion forints in unpaid broadcasting fees by national radio and television.
AH received another 2.5 billion cash injection from APV in the form of equity increase mid-December.
Kiss said the broadcasting infrastructure developments call for an investment of four billion forints and the government will decide this year how to provide the remaining 1.5 billion.
"This could be in the form of a privatisation coupled with a capital increase, or it could be some other way," Kiss told Reuters.
He added that the government has not yet decided on AH's privatisation strategy, which analysts believe will only happen once the radio and TV-channels have been privatised.
The head of radio and TV watchdog ORTT, Mihaly Revesz said earlier he would be against privatising both the channels and the broadcasting infrastructure.
The concession fee Hungary asked for the two TV-channels on offer is a minimum eight billion forints per channel per year (plus VAT at 25 percent).
